note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent auditor). RFC 4271 Section 4.3: "They MUST be zero when sent and MUST be ignored when received." Receive clause: TestRFC4271AttrFlagsLowNibbleIgnoredOnReceive asserts RFC7606ActionNone for ORIGIN/AS_PATH/NEXT_HOP flagged 0x4F; TestRFC4271RelayedLowNibbleClearedOnBothRails asserts ActionNone for the same plus unknown 241 at 0xCF and that the route is relayed; the .ci shows the route installed and relayed to an rs-client and an eBGP peer. Send clause: the same relay unit and .ci assert every relayed flags octet has bits 0-3 zero with exact octets (0x40, 0xE0), over writeUpdateBody's normalizeTransmittedUpdate, the funnel of every writer. Negative TestRFC4271AttrFlagsHighBitsNotIgnored: with the low nibble set, a wrong Optional or Transitive bit on ORIGIN still yields TreatAsWithdraw AttrCode 1, red on a validator that ignores the whole octet. Minor: that unit's comment says 0x4F carries Extended Length; it does not (0x4F &^ 0x10 == 0x4F), which changes no assertion. Re-judged again 2026-10-14 after 78f4d4e160 added a '# malformed-frame:' comment above the .ci send frame: comment only, skipped by the peer and runner readers, so the received frame (ORIGIN/AS_PATH/NEXT_HOP 0x4F, 241 0xCF) and both exact relay expectations are unchanged. A validator that stopped ignoring the low nibble would treat-as-withdraw on ORIGIN 0x4F and the conn 2/3 expectations would go red. The .ci shows acceptance through relay; it does not read the RIB itself. Verdict unchanged.
